The PFMS also interfaces with higher-level systems, including supervisory control and data acquisition and tertiary control systems, such as Verrus’ optimal dispatch engine, but these are not a focus of this report and hence are shown as dotted interfaces in Figure 1. The complexity, scale, and novelty of the PFMS and Verrus’ data center power system calls for a rigorous validation and de-risking of the integrated power system before field deployment. With this intent, Verrus collaborated with NREL to develop the Vulcan test platform, which uses a CHIL-based validation of the PFMS integrated with a digital real-time simulation (DRTS) of the data center power system, as shown in Figure 1. A CHIL framework enables the validation of the sequence of operations for a wide collection of system states and operating scenarios. The DRTS can model and simulate power system components in the electromagnetic transient domain in real time. This allows DRTS users to perform a suite of experiments that is typically called a CHIL framework [4]. A CHIL framework leverages the ability of the DRTS to model electromagnetic transient models and run them in real time to generate power system states, such as voltage and current signals (analog), circuit breaker status/control (digital), and the PFMS response/control actions in the form of set points/ discrete inputs. The CHIL setup can be used to leverage the analog and digital input-output through network-based open communication protocol cards on the DRTS platform to execute closed-loop experiments with the PFMS [5]. To evaluate the PFMS in a CHIL framework, the data center power system is modeled in a DRTS plat- form, and the PFMS is connected to the DRTS model using Distributed Network Protocol 3 (DNP3). This setup constitutes a closed-loop framework and allows for the evaluation of the sequence of operations in the PFMS device. In summary, the Vulcan test platform comprises the following: 1. The data center power system, which is being modeled using the DRTS at NREL (part of NREL’s ARIES virtual emulation environment). The data center power system is described in detail in Section 3. 2. A real-time automation controller using DNP3 connected as a communication device between the PFMS and the DRTS 3. The Verrus-developed PFMS, which is integrated with the real-time automation controller and uses DNP3 as the communication protocol to exchange data. Further details on the PFMS and its algorithms are described in Section 4.
